Creation to handover

the cost is paid up front, in seconds; the return arrives four years later, in weeks
4CREATE
90 sone decision
Pick a discipline template. That single choice sets the required metadata for the next four years, and inherits the grant and ethics record.
Skip it and every dataset arrives with whatever metadata the uploader felt like typing that afternoon.

2THE CONTAINER
4 yearscontinuous
Everything lands here: 26 artifacts, 14 discussions, the grant and the ethics record. Testers asked for exactly this — one place where data, publications and discussion sit together.
Skip it and the same work scatters across a shared drive, a chat thread and three inboxes.

5THE RECORD
+2 minper experiment day
Append-only entries linking protocol, sample, instrument and raw data. Two minutes a day is the entire price of the handover at the far end.
Skip it and there is no defensible record of what was run — and no way to tell a lot problem from an operator one.

9WHEN IT BREAKS
6 daystracked, not forgotten
An issue anchored to a protocol step, with a named blocker and a date. Three of the lab's issues have closed as published null results — the failure became the output.
Skip it and the same assay fails for the next three people, each discovering it alone.

22HANDOVER
40 minnot two weeks
94% compiles itself. The 40 minutes is one recorded interview answering six questions generated from what the record could not supply.
This is Dr Laurent's entire business case, and it is only true because steps 4, 2, 5 and 9 happened.

THE ARITHMETIC OF THE WHOLE DOMAIN
up-front cost · template choice90 s, once
running cost · notebook, 4 years≈ 22 h total
handover, structured40 min
handover, unstructured · what happens today2 weeks, mostly guessing
Twenty-two hours of notebook writing spread across four years buys back two weeks at the end — and, far more valuable, it buys back the 148 datasets a successor can actually use.
THE ORDER MATTERS
Every step is cheap only because the previous one happened. The template makes metadata automatic; metadata makes notebook links possible; the links make an issue anchorable; anchored issues make the handover a query rather than an interrogation. Remove step 4 and the cost does not vanish — it lands on step 22, quadrupled.
WHAT THIS FLOW DOES NOT CLAIM
It does not claim a researcher fills in metadata because it is good for the institution. They fill it in because the template already asked, at the one moment they were creating something and had the answer in front of them. Every screen in domain G is built on that single principle — ask while the answer is in the room.
